clue.text: People who could weep for London?

definitions.text: People who could weep for London?

parts.words: People who could weep for London?
parts.note: read 'weep for London' as shouting out on behalf of a place where people live: old-time public announcers did exactly that for their borough

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about who might shed tears over the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weep' is the misleader: the other sense of 'cry' is to call out loudly, and London stands for any town or city whose news these officials once shouted in the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic public announcers rang a bell and called out news and proclamations through a municipality's streets.

clue.text: Nailed by diplomatic report

indicators.note: a report is a sound heard, so the clue word's synonym is said out loud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: someone diplomatic has tact, the noun for that quality

explanation.surface: Something pinned down thanks to an envoy's dispatch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like the diplomat's dispatch but signals a homophone: TACT, said out loud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small nails with broad heads are tacks, so fastening with them is a synonym of nailing.

clue.text: Originally, why only men bought action toys — or an animal!

indicators.note: originally points at how each of the following words begins, so their opening letters are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A grumble about why action figures were bought only by men, or perhaps it was a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing Australian marsupial is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Sport for an angry nation?

parts.note: cross means angry
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A question about which game a furious nation would play.
explanation.definitionFit: Running over open fields and hills rather than a track is a recognised athletic sport.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about one new Tory taking 50 per ceent

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: taking fifty per cent of the following word means keeping its first half, two of its four letters

explanation.surface: A fresh Conservative candidate keen on taking half of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ceent' is the clue's own typo for 'cent'. Half of TORY, its first two letters, gives TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keen on a hobby is informally being into it, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Caller accepts fix — the paperwork is there!

indicators.note: accepts means one word takes another into its middle

parts.note: a ringer is one who rings, i.e. a caller on the phone or a bell-ringer
to bind is to fix or fasten

explanation.surface: Someone on the phone accepts a predicament, pointing to where the documents are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a noun meaning a jam, but here it is the verb 'bind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose-leaf folder with metal hoops is where office papers are kept.

clue.text: The sort of man to back influential people?

indicators.note: to back here means to put into reverse, so the abbreviation is read from the end

parts.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of fellow would support people with clout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To back' looks like supporting, but it signals a reversal. A SPIV is British slang for a flashy petty dealer in black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide boy trading in shady goods is a type of man the clue loosely describes.

clue.text: The garden of Eden is found in a row of shops!

indicators.note: found in means the short word sits inside the longer one

parts.note: a parade in British usage is a row of shops along a street

explanation.surface: Claims the biblical garden can be located on a high street.
explanation.walkthrough: A PARADE is the British term for a short row of shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the heavenly garden of Genesis, commonly called a paradise.

clue.text: Reproduce live data so as to confirm

indicators.note: reproduce means the letters are produced again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions to replicate real-time figures to verify a finding.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratify or corroborate something is a synonym of confirming it.

clue.text: Arriving outside, keep giving reassurance

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps round the other

parts.note: coming means arriving
a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort

explanation.surface: Someone turns up and, standing outside, keeps offering consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a castle's central tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Soothing words that ease worry are consoling, which is what reassurance does.

clue.text: Examination that some take for a laugh?

indicators.note: some take means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Suggests some people sit a test purely for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'fOR A Laugh'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in language exams, is a type of examination.

clue.text: Blood test out, hence got dressed

indicators.note: dressed means arranged or put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A blood test is done, so the patient puts their clothes back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood' looks like a noun for the test, but it is the verb meaning to give a first experience.
explanation.definitionFit: To blood a newcomer is to initiate them, and the idiom for gaining first experience means the same.

clue.text: Run out after mistake by bridge player

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: East is one of the four players in bridge, abbreviated E
a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A card player makes an error and time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so any of N, S, E, W can be a 'bridge player'.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that passes until it is gone has expired, like a term running out.

clue.text: Leapt onto answer — it was "plentiful"!

indicators.note: onto means the second piece is set immediately after the first

parts.note: bounded means leapt or jumped

explanation.surface: Someone jumped on a reply which was said to be ample.
explanation.definitionFit: If something existed in great quantities it was abundant, the past tense matching 'it was plentiful'.

clue.text: An indication of possessiveness?

parts.note: read possessiveness not as jealousy but as the grammatical possessive, and ask which punctuation mark signals it

explanation.surface: Asks for a sign that someone is jealously clingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possessiveness' suggests a jealous partner; it means the possessive case in grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: The mark added before s in 'the cat's bowl' shows ownership in English grammar.

clue.text: Partner prepared to stand by the fire

parts.note: a companion is a partner
set means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: A partner gets ready to stand beside the hearth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a holder for fireside tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker, tongs and brush hang from a holder beside the hearth, a fireside tool set on a stand.

clue.text: How to fill out hair so it can't get free?

parts.note: to pad is to fill out with extra material
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: Asks how to bulk up a hairstyle so it stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Detachable shackled locks fasten a gate or chain so it cannot be opened.

clue.text: Cocoons one who gives birth aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means inside a vessel, so the word goes within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a mother is one who gives birth

explanation.surface: A woman delivers a baby on a ship and wraps it up warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: SS is the prefix for a steamship, hence a 'ship' in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrapping someone up thickly and protectively is to envelop them, as a pupa is cocooned.

clue.text: Controlled diet? In dreams!

annotationWithheld.why: Controlled diet? In dreams! (12): the answer is an anagram of DIET IN DREAMS, which uses every word but 'Controlled', so no word is left to signal the anagram unless 'Controlled' is both definition and indicator.

clue.text: Searches following dangers

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
risks are dangers

explanation.surface: Investigations that come after hazards are identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ff' or 'f' after a page number means 'and following', hence F.
explanation.definitionFit: Police patting down a suspect's clothes are searching them.

clue.text: Standard writer (not French)

parts.note: a pen is something that writes
non is French for not

explanation.surface: An ordinary author who is not from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective meaning ordinary; here it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow flag carried on a lance is a kind of standard, a banner.

clue.text: Sort of retail lines that are bookish?

indicators.note: sort means put in order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: RY is short for railway, which runs on lines

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of shop lines appeal to readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like 'kind of' but is the anagram signal on RETAIL, giving LITERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fond of books and learning is studious, the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: About five, look to go without food

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: At about five o'clock someone gazes and skips a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About five' looks like a time; 'About' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Going hungry for a long time is to be deprived of nourishment.

clue.text: Girl who wrote article on Northumberland?

indicators.note: on means one piece sits on top of the other in a down entry

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Northumberland is a county in north-east England, NE for short

explanation.surface: Asks about a young woman who wrote a piece about a northern English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland lies in England's North East, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Frank, the young diarist, and Anne Brontë, the novelist, are famous female writers.

clue.text: How to eat cold chop?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
to hew is to chop

explanation.surface: Asks the way to consume a cold lamb chop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop' looks like a cut of meat, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding food with the teeth is a way of eating it.

clue.text: Period when swans may be captured by a noose, perhaps?

indicators.note: captured by means the word is held inside another set of letters
perhaps hints that the following letters are only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

parts.note: pens are female swans

explanation.surface: Asks when swans might be legally snared with a loop of rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swans' reads as birds being hunted, but it is the crossword staple for female swans; 'captured by' puts them inside the rearrangement of 'a noose' that 'perhaps' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The months when hunting a given game is permitted make up a time of year, a span.

clue.text: Special forces hospital band

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A military hospital's musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' suggests musicians; it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of fabric worn round the waist or over the shoulder is a type of band.

clue.text: One's led her astray wearing this!

definitions.text: One's led her astray wearing this!

indicators.note: astray means led off course, so the letters wander into another order

parts.note: taken as one is, contributing its four letters

explanation.surface: A man has seduced a woman while dressed in alpine shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a Bavarian who led her astray might be wearing these leather shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional Bavarian leather breeches are the garment a Tyrolean seducer would wear.
